title: Percent Change
objective: After this level you can work out how much something rose or fell in percent by comparing the change with where it started.
summary: Percent change is the change divided by the starting value. A $5 rise is 25% on a $20 ticket but only 1% on a $500 phone, and a fall from $25 to $20 is 20%.

cards.headline: A $20 ticket goes up $5. Is that a lot? It depends where you started.
cards.body: Five dollars on a $20 ticket feels steep. The same five dollars on a $500 phone barely registers. Percent change is the tool that tells those two apart.

cards.headline: Change divided by start
cards.body: To find a percent change, first find the change: new minus old. Then divide it by where you started, and turn the answer into a percent. The ticket went from $20 to $25, a change of $5. And 5 ÷ 20 = 0.25, so the price rose 25%.

cards.headline: Same $5, different story
cards.body: Now the phone: $500 up to $505. The change is still $5, but 5 ÷ 500 is just 0.01, a 1% rise. The starting value is the ruler you measure the change against. A small start makes a big percent; a big start makes a small one. So whenever you hear "up 25%", ask the follow-up: up from what?

cards.fact: Falling works the same way, measured from where the fall began.
cards.context: A $25 ticket cut back to $20 has dropped $5, and 5 ÷ 25 = 0.2: a 20% fall. Same $5 as the rise, but this time it's measured against $25, a bigger start, so the percent is smaller. Tuck that away. It's the whole secret of the next level.

questions.prompt: To find a percent change, what do you divide the change by?

options.label: The new value
options.rationale: Percent change always measures against where you started.
You divide by the start, then express the answer as a percent.

options.label: The average of old and new
options.rationale: Percent change uses the starting value, not an average.

questions.explanation: Percent change = (new minus old) ÷ starting value, written as a percent.

questions.prompt: A $20 ticket and a $500 phone each go up $5. Why are their percent changes so different?

options.label: Phones are measured in a different unit
options.rationale: Both are dollars; only the starting values differ.

options.label: Percent change ignores the size of the change
options.rationale: It uses the change, divided by the start.

options.label: Only the ticket really changed price
Each $5 is divided by a different starting price

questions.explanation: Percent change divides the change by the start: 5 ÷ 20 is 25%, but 5 ÷ 500 is only 1%.

questions.prompt: The ticket's price rose 25%. Using Level 2's meaning of percent, how much did it rise for every $100 of its old price?

options.rationale: That was the actual rise on a $20 ticket, not per $100.
That would be the new price per $100, not the rise.

questions.explanation: Percent means out of every 100, so a 25% rise is $25 for every $100 of the starting price.
